fischbach-contributions: Section 1, p.2: the authors list their own contributions and target audience.
fischbach-circuit-opt-classes: Section 1 p.1 and Section 3.2.3 p.7: the authors define the two classes they use; the logical-qubit-level wording is on p.7 and the device-mapping wording on p.1.
fischbach-graph-like-definition: Definition 4.1, p.8: the five conditions match the value.
fischbach-rewrite-rule-definition: Definition 4.2, p.9: r : ZX -> ZX with gamma(g) = (gamma o r)(g); matches the value.
fischbach-optimization-pipeline: Section 4.3.1, p.9 to 10: the paper defines its own idealized three-step pipeline (Convert, Search, Extraction) used to organize the survey.
fischbach-causal-flow-definition: Definition 4.5, p.11 to 12: g : V\O -> V\I with conditions v < g(v), neighbours of g(v) are v or follow v, v in N(g(v)); matches the value. It is a definition, so the paper's later sufficient/necessary wording does not affect it.
fischbach-general-flow-definition: Definition 4.6, p.12: g maps to correction sets, plane labels XY/XZ/YZ, five conditions with the odd neighbourhood; the value states only the structure and matches it. The paper's own sufficient (p.2, p.11) against necessary (p.12) wording for general flow is not part of this definition.
fischbach-review-scope: Abstract, p.1: the authors state their own scope; the value matches the quote word for word.
fischer-du-gate-definition: Dual unitary circuits, p.2 (and Methods, p.5, which gives the dual operator formally): the paper defines DU gates in the quoted sentence.
fischer-model-setup: p.2: the paper states the Hamiltonian, the kick, the brickwork circuit and the native ZX/ECR interaction as its own model and hardware.
fischer-brickwork-mapping: SI I A, p.11 to 12, Eqs. (S1) to (S9): an algebraic derivation in the paper (commuting h-gates and J-gates, Sigma^dagger U Sigma = U_KI U_KI), with no cited step. The statement about the periods follows from it.
fischer-system-sizes-params: Results, p.4, and SI Table I, p.15: h values {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15} and sizes 51, 71, 91 match the paper's own experiment table.
fischer-device: SI II A, p.14: ibm strasbourg, 127 fixed-frequency transmons, heavy-hexagonal lattice, median T1 315 us and T2 187 us, as the paper states for its own device.
fischer-circuit-execution: SI II B, p.14: uniform Pauli twirling of ECR layers, twirled measurement by X or identity, randomised X/Y/Z bases for IC data, parametric compilation through the Sampler primitive. Matches the value.
fischer-ic-measurements-basis-bias: Results, p.4: the 80/10/10 bias on the signal qubit and uniform sampling elsewhere are the paper's own measurement design. The reason given ('dominated by the X-contribution') is the authors' stated rationale for that design.
fischer-noise-model-learning: Results, p.4 and Methods, p.5 to 6: the paper states its own noise-learning procedure (twirling, sparse Pauli-Lindblad model, use of the h = 0 Clifford data to fix extra degrees of freedom). 'Novel' is the authors' word for their own extension; the value attributes it to them.
fischer-tem-bond-dim-91: Results, p.5: chi = 70 for N = 91 is the paper's own setting. The second sentence is a stated caveat on TEM's accuracy in general, which the authors place on their own approach. Both parts rest on the paper's own statement.
fischer-spam-gauge-caveat: SI II D, p.19: the authors state that their fidelity-split learning is no longer independent of SPAM errors, because twirled readout mitigation assumes perfect state preparation, and that the individual fidelities cannot be amplified. A limit on their own noise learning.
fischer-noise-learning-circuits: SI II D, p.17: depths {0,2,6,12,20,34}, 64 twirling instances, 32 shots per instance, 9 initial-state settings. Matches the value.
fischer-mitigation-bias-from-noise-model: SI III G, p.27, and Results p.4: the authors state that a mismatch between learned and actual noise biases the mitigated results, and that deep circuits accumulate a non-negligible difference. A limit on their own method.
fischer-competing-interests: p.7: a disclosure the paper makes about itself (patent applications by Algorithmiq Oy). Not a result. It is the paper's own statement of a fact about the work.
fischer-accuracy-limits-correlators-only: Results, p.5: the authors state that away from the DU point the expectation values are not autocorrelation functions and can only be checked against approximate classical methods. A limit on their own verification.
rydberggpt-system-setup: Section II, p.1 to 2: 'We consider a system of N = L x L atoms arranged on a square lattice', with qubits encoded in the ground and Rydberg states. The paper's own setup.
rydberggpt-thermal-noise-setup: Section II, p.2: 'for the purposes of our study, the atom array is considered to be affected by thermal noise, in equilibrium at a temperature T = 1/beta'. The paper's own modelling choice.
rydberggpt-graph-nn-compression: Section III, p.2 to 3: the paper states its own encoder design (graph neural network to a linear-size sequence, then a vanilla transformer encoder to the context vector). The scaling sentence is a plain count of edges against nodes.
rydberggpt-model-size: Table I, p.3, checked on the rendered page: d_ff 128, d_model 32, d_graph 64, 8 heads, 1 encoder block, 3 decoder blocks, 2 graph layers, 66562 trainable parameters. The order in the value matches the table.
rydberggpt-training-data-source: Section IV, p.3: the target sequences are simulated by SSE quantum Monte Carlo and the dataset is called synthetic. The paper's own data source.
rydberggpt-training-parameter-grid: Section IV, p.3, checked on the rendered page: beta Omega {0.5,1,2,4,8,16}, delta/Omega in [-0.364, 3.173], Rb/a {1.05,1.15,1.3}, L {5,6,11,12,15,16}.
rydberggpt-three-model-split: Section IV, p.3: M1 on L = 5, 6; M2 on L = 5, 6, 11, 12; M3 on all six sizes; all at Rb/a = 1.15. The paper's own experiment design.
rydberggpt-training-compute: Section IV, p.3 and Table III caption, p.4: a single A100 GPU, 85 hours, a constant time per model.
rydberggpt-dataset-bias-by-size: Section IV, p.3; Section V B, p.5 (checked on the rendered pages): 10^5 samples per lattice size, so larger sizes have more tokens, and the dataset is biased towards larger lattice sizes (Table II). Correct the value: the rendered number is 10^5 (ten to the fifth), not 105.
rydberggpt-finite-temperature-invalid: Section V A, p.4 and Section V B, p.5: the authors state that the decoder-as-amplitude reading is not valid at finite temperature and that Psi_theta does not capture the thermal state, and they point to their Figure 3 as the demonstration.
rydberggpt-fig2-setup: Section V B, p.4 (checked on the rendered page): M1, Rb/a = 1.15, beta Omega = 16.0, N_s = 10^5 samples, benchmarked against 10^5 decorrelated QMC samples taken as ground truth. Correct the value: the number is 10^5, not 105.
rydberggpt-fewer-samples-fig4: Section V B, p.5 (checked on the rendered page): Figure 4 energies from M1, M2, M3, averaged over 10^4 samples. Correct the value: the number is 10^4, not 104.
rydberggpt-open-source-release: Section VI, p.7 and the abstract: the paper states that the code and model weights are available at [59].
rydberggpt-architecture: Abstract, p.1 and Section III, p.2 to 3: the paper states the encoder-decoder architecture it builds, its input (the interacting Hamiltonian) and its output (autoregressive measurement probabilities).
fontana-def-periodic-ansatz-dla: Definition 2.1 and Eqs. (1) and (2), p.2: the paper defines the periodic ansatz, the dynamical Lie group and the DLA (naming it as in [28]).
fontana-def-trainable: Section 2 A, p.2: the paper states the terms untrainable (a PQC with a BP) and trainable (variance Omega(1/poly(n))).
fontana-def-lasa: Definition 2.4, p.2: LASA is a periodic ansatz with iO in the DLA. Matches the value.
fontana-def-abstracted-gradient: Definition 2.5, p.3: the abstracted gradient is defined. The link to the PQC gradient follows at once by differentiating e^(-theta H), as the paper notes.
fontana-no-full-basis-relaxation: Appendix H, p.38 to 39: the authors state it is unclear if the full orthogonal-basis assumption can be relaxed. The 'numerical evidence appears' phrase is their hedge, cited to [22], and qualifies the limit.
fontana-two-design-may-fail: Section 2 C, p.4: the authors state there may be settings (other initializations, correlated parameters) where the 2-design assumption fails and their results do not hold. The remark on evidence [35, 36] is a hedge on that limit.
fontana-gradvar-definition-mean-zero: Eqs. (13) and (14), p.4 define GradVar. Lemma C.1, p.20: for a compact Lie group and any representation the first moment is zero. The proof (Haar invariance, then differentiating e^(theta H)) is in the paper.
fontana-theorem-2-8-simple-group: Theorem 2.8, p.4 to 5, with its conditions (compact connected simple G, finite-dimensional unitary representation, iO = dphi(o), H = dphi(h)). Proved in Section 4 B, p.10 to 11 using Lemma 4.1 (proved as Lemma C.2 with Schur orthogonality, a textbook tool).
fontana-theorem-2-9-compact-group: Theorem 2.9, p.4 to 5: stated with its conditions. Proved in Section 4 C, p.11 from Lemma 4.2 (proved as Lemma C.3 by Schur orthogonality). The proof is short, but each step is given.
fontana-lemma-4-1-4-2: Lemma 4.1 and 4.2, p.10 to 11; proofs are Lemmas C.2 and C.3, p.20 to 21, by Schur orthogonality (textbook, [47 Cor. 4.10]).
fontana-theorem-2-12-superposition: Theorem 2.12, p.6, proof in Section 4 E, p.12: the computation of the projected norm (n-1)/8 and the result n(n-1)/(16(n^2-1)^2) is in the paper, and I checked the algebra. Note the proof fixes O = i h^z_12 with norm^2 1/2, so the scaling holds for observables in the DLA of fixed norm.
fontana-theorem-2-13-bp: Theorem 2.13, p.7 and Theorem D.3, p.22 to 24: stated with its conditions (n even, middle Hamming weight, rank-one projector onto another basis state) and proved in the SI using Lemma D.1, the dimension in Lemma D.2 (checked at n = 2 and n = 4) and textbook Schur-Weyl, Pieri and Jacobi-Trudi tools. The bound it proves, O(1/dim V_lambda0), is stronger than the stated one.
fontana-numerics-setup: Appendix G, p.34: Qulacs, brick architecture, L = 12n layers, parameters in [0, 4 pi), finite-difference gradients, 5000 samples for n < 18 and 1000 for n >= 18, rescaling by 1/4. All stated by the paper as its own setup.
fontana-theorem-e2-lower-bound: Theorem E.2, p.26 and proof p.26 to 27, with Lemma E.1: proved in the paper from the Cartan-Weyl form of the split Casimir (textbook), and the steps check. The printed statement has a typo (||rho_g||_F where the proof has the squared norm). The remark that the weight norm is hard to determine is a stated practical limit.
fontana-appendix-f-zero-variance-example: Appendix F, p.29: the two-qubit example is computed in the paper (Eqs. F16, F17): the cost is zero for every group element, so the variance is zero. I checked the calculation. The remark that the state is not the cause is correct by the same calculation.
franco-review-question: Abstract, p.1: the authors state the question and scope of their own review.
franco-scope-quantum-assisted-ml: Section II B, p.2: the authors state they concentrate on quantum-assisted ML; the PQC description is the paper's own characterization of that subfield.
franco-noise-as-adversary: Section II B 3, p.3: the sentence is the paper's own framing of what viewing noise as an adversarial act means. The comparison to fault injections cites [20] but is part of the same framing sentence.
franco-methodology-prisma: Section III, p.3: the paper states its own search method, PRISMA as a guideline and the two parts (systematic, narrative snowballing).
franco-arxiv-manual-search: Section III, p.3: the authors state their arXiv search was manual and heuristic because of the missing API and volume, which restricted scraping. A limit on their own method.
franco-selection-criteria: Section III, p.3: inclusion and exclusion criteria as the paper states them; the value matches.
franco-search-sources: Table I, p.3: the sources listed match the value. Figure 1 lists a slightly different set (it adds NPJ QI), but the value reports Table I as stated.
franco-scoring-scheme: Section III A, p.4: score is twice the term's list position, doubled with Quantum, +200 for Table IV combinations, -300 for Table III terms, penalties set by repeated analysis of the top 50. Matches the value.
franco-filtering-counts: Section III A, p.4 and Figure 1: 4,658 - 142 - 1,193 - 2,323 = 1,000, and the text and Figure 1 agree on every number in this value.
franco-physical-attacks-excluded: Section III A, p.4: the authors state the exclusion of literature needing physical hardware manipulation or attacks with a direct classical analogue. Stated as their own scope.
franco-vulnerability-categories: Section IV, p.4: both categories are defined by the paper in its own words; the value matches.
franco-defense-categories: Section V, p.5: the paper collects defenses under the three areas and defines formal verification in the quoted sentence.
review-27-records: Section III A, p.4 and Figure 1: both the text and Figure 1 give 4,658 records identified and 27 included, so the two numbers in the value agree across the paper. Caution for the team lead: the text's intermediate chain (92 screened, 25 + 7 + 4) does not add to 27, while Figure 1 (23 + 4) does. The value does not rely on that chain. Basis is setup, not 'proved result' as the reader suggested.

theory_low.fischbach-25-general-flows: Section 4.4.2, p.12 to 13: 'it can be shown' that Figure 8b admits 25 flows, but the enumeration is not shown, and the claim about 8c rests on the absence of flow meaning non-deterministic. The paper calls general flow 'sufficient' on p.11 and 'necessary' on p.12. Both cannot hold, so the 8c conclusion is not settled. An example claim, not a proved theorem.
theory_low.fischer-autocorrelator-exact: Eq. (2), p.3: the paper says 'can be calculated exactly [12]' and cites Bertini, Kos, Prosen. SI I B (p.12 to 13) derives only the n = t case, and it equates its result to Ref. [12]'s expression. The n not equal t branch (zero) is 'easy to show' with no argument. The conditions N odd and t <= (N-1)/2 are not argued in the SI. The full value is not proved here.
theory_low.fischer-lightcone-decay: p.3: this follows from Eq. (2), which rests on Ref. [12] and is not fully proved here (the zero outside the light cone is argued from causality in words and 'easy to show'). Decay at h not 0 follows from cos^t(2h) only if Eq. (2) holds.
theory_low.fischer-expectation-reduction: p.3 and SI I B, p.12 to 13: the SI shows the equivalence for n = t by diagrams, but states that the final expression 'is identical to the one given in Ref. [12]', where identity initial states are used, and then concludes equivalence. This uses Ref. [12]. The off-boundary case is 'easy to show' with no argument.
theory_low.fischer-supp-derivation: SI I B, p.13, Eqs. (S11) to (S14): the matrix M_U and the cos^t(2h) result are computed in the paper, but they equal Cn(t) only through the equivalence with Ref. [12]'s infinite-temperature expression, which is taken from that paper. The quotes also drop the conditions (J = b = pi/4, N odd, t <= (N-1)/2).
theory_low.fischer-heisenberg-clifford-perturbation: Methods, p.7: 'can be attributed to' is the authors' interpretation of the simulation convergence. 'chi = 1 suffices' at the Clifford point is stated without a proof. Not a proved result.
theory_low.fischer-tem-typicality: SI III E, p.26: the claim that the experiment goes beyond typicality, and the Pauli weights 2 and about 10, are read from the authors' own classical simulations. A measured or simulated result, with no proof.
theory_low.fischer-tem-variance-limit: SI III E, p.26: the exponential variance in the Pauli weight is cited to [66], and is a limit of a conventional measurement method, not of the authors' own work. The Pauli-weight reduction is the authors' method and is not shown here. Cited result.
theory_low.rydberggpt-local-estimator-derivation: Appendix A, p.9: the derivation is in the paper and is standard (the variational Monte Carlo local estimator). But the value and quotes drop its conditions: Psi_theta = sqrt(p_theta) real and positive, a purely off-diagonal O for the C_O form, and that the average is over samples (an approximation). Not stated with its conditions.
theory_low.fontana-lasa-includes-hva-qaoa: Section 2 B, p.3: that LASAs include HVA and QAOA (cited [29], [2, 30]) and that all LASAs are EQNNs (cited [31]) is asserted with a brief informal reason. It is not proved here and part of it rests on cited work.
theory_low.fontana-theorem-2-6-mixing: Theorem 2.6, p.4 and Theorem H.1 and Corollary H.2.1, p.34 to 39: the proof 'roughly follows' Ref. [33] and relies on the spectral-gap to t-design link from [34, 59]. It takes 'WLOG simple' without argument, and H.2.1 is 'one can see'. Theorem 2.6 also drops the irreducibility condition that Theorem H.1 needs. A proof that uses other papers' results as steps, so LOW.
theory_low.fontana-theorem-h1-t-design: Theorem H.1 and Lemma H.2, p.34 to 38: the proof follows Ref. [33] (the A_n case 'reproduces the result of Ref. [33]') and uses the spectral-gap framework of [34, 59]. Several steps are 'one can verify'. The reduction to a simple algebra is not argued. Cited results as proof steps.
theory_low.fontana-killing-norm-bound: Lemma C.4, p.21: the proof asserts ||[H,E_k]||_F^2 <= 2||H||_F^2 with no justification for the norm bound. The quotes carry only the sentence that Conjecture 2.3 is 'explicitly proven (and significantly generalized)', which is the authors' interpretation. Eq. (19) gives 1/d_{g_alpha} per ideal, not obviously 1/poly(d_g) when ideals are small.
theory_low.fontana-bp-conditions: Section 2 E, p.5: 'we infer that a BP can only occur whenever...' is the authors' reading of Eq. (18). The 'novel prediction' sentence is their claim. Not a theorem.
theory_low.fontana-theorem-2-10-compound-mixing: Theorem 2.10, p.6 and Corollary H.2.2, p.39: it follows from Theorem H.1, which is graded LOW (it uses Ref. [33]). The paper admits the angles for the sum-of-Z generators are not independent, and 'one can check' that the set is an orthogonal basis of the DLA.
theory_low.fontana-theorem-2-11-basis-state: Theorem 2.11, p.6 and proof p.11 to 12: the proof gives GradVar = k(n-k)/(2(n^2-1)^2) for O = i h^z_12. At Hamming weight k = 0 or n this is zero, so the statement 'for a computational basis state ... Omega(1/n^3)' is false there. The statement drops the condition 1 <= k <= n-1. It also fixes no observable, and the proof uses one.
theory_low.fontana-corollary-2-12-1-single-qubit: Corollary 2.12.1, p.7 and proof p.12: the computational-basis-state case follows by Cauchy-Schwarz (I checked it), but it needs k between 1 and n-1 (at k = 0 the variance is zero). The uniform-superposition case is 'a similar result can be shown', with no argument. 'Answers an open question of [27]' is a claim.
theory_low.fontana-heisenberg-picture-advantage: Section 2 G, p.7 to 8: the claim that earlier Schrodinger-picture approaches meet 'significant obstacles' and that this approach 'completely circumvents' them is the authors' assessment of the literature and of their method. Not a scope statement.
theory_low.fontana-compactness-note: Section 4 A, p.9: that any subalgebra of su(2^n) is a sum of compact simple algebras and a center is cited ([38, 47]). 'Harmless to ignore the center' is given as a one-line reason, not shown.
theory_low.fontana-lemma-d1-d2: Lemmas D.1 and D.2, p.22 to 23: D.2 is computed (I checked it at n = 2 and n = 4). D.1 is a sketch ('One can verify'), and it is stated for any Hamming weight k while the partition lambda0 = (2,...,2) with n/2 rows is only right for k = n/2. The value covers both.
theory_low.fontana-theorem-f3-outside-dla: Theorem F.3, p.29 and proof p.32 to 33: the proof is condensed ('we already know...') and rests on Lemmas F.4 to F.6. The value also says the bound shows decay with DLA dimension 'can still appear' for observables outside the DLA. That is the authors' reading, and the added covariance terms may be negative.
theory_low.fontana-non-ideal-complement: Appendix F, p.33 to 34: 'can have no dependence on the dimension of the DLA' follows from the exact formula only in outline, and 'all scenarios are possible' is speculation with no example or proof. It is not a limit the authors state on a result.
theory_low.fontana-appendix-b-recovers-known: Appendix B, p.19 to 20: the paper evaluates its formula in three cases and says each 'agrees with' Eq. 13 or the result of [22]. The cited results are not reproduced here, so the agreement is the authors' claim.
theory_low.fontana-methods-adjoint-trick: Section 4 A, p.9: the observation that the second-moment integral is an adjoint-representation integral is a heuristic that makes the scaling 'more plausible'. The statement that approximate 2-designs for SU(2^n) have BPs is cited [18, 22]. Neither is a proved result at this point.
theory_low.fontana-lasa-gradient-variance-inverse-d: Narrowed value is better: it carries the paper's own caveat (Section 2 B, p.2) that DLA dimension may not dominate. The rigorous results are Theorems 2.8 and 2.9 (exact formula, graded HIGH). 'Scales inversely with the dimension of the DLA' is the authors' interpretation of that formula and holds only if the norm factors are O(1), which the paper itself says may fail.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.fontana-rapid-mixing-polynomial-dla: Narrowed value is better: it carries the orthogonal-basis and uniform-draw conditions of Theorem 2.6. The result rests on Theorem H.1, which follows Ref. [33], uses [34, 59], and has several 'one can verify' steps, so LOW. 'To motivate' is the authors' purpose.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)

value_replace.rydberggpt-dataset-bias-by-size: The authors state that because they generate one hundred thousand samples for each lattice size (the text layer prints the exponent flat, as 105), the larger lattice sizes have more tokens than the smaller ones, so the dataset is biased towards larger lattice sizes.
value_replace.rydberggpt-fig2-setup: The authors state that the first results figure shows a model at Rb/a = 1.15 and βΩ = 16.0, with estimators benchmarked against the QMC observables calculated from one hundred thousand decorrelated samples (the text layer prints the exponent flat, as 105), which they take as the ground truth.
value_replace.rydberggpt-fewer-samples-fig4: The authors state that the energy evaluations in Figure 4 are averaged over ten thousand samples (the text layer prints the exponent flat, as 104), from each of the three trained models.
